name: Exactly Protocol DebtManager unvalidated-market impersonation
summary: DebtManager accepted a caller-supplied market in its permit and leverage path without checking that the Auditor listed it. A malicious market bypassed the permit, set DebtManager's effective sender to a victim, then reentered crossDeleverage with a real market to withdraw the victim's position through an attacker-controlled swap pool.

loss.notes: Exactly's post-mortem reports $7,612,038 lost by 117 accounts. The main attacker caused 97% of the campaign loss and a copycat using the same defect caused the remaining 3%.

ageReset.description: The proxy creation transaction emitted Upgraded selecting the vulnerable DebtManager implementation; no later Upgraded event occurred before the exploit.

sources.note: Reviewed the live Optimism receipt and call trace, the implementation and proxy creation traces, the proxy implementation slot, every Upgraded event through the exploit, the pre-exploit implementation hash, the exact commit-matching verified source, and Exactly's post-mortem. The attacker contract calls DebtManager proxy 0x675d410dcf6f343219aae8d1dde0bfab46f52106, which repeatedly delegatecalls 0x16748cb753a68329ca2117a7647aa590317ebf41. The unvalidated market and permit path lets malicious market contracts make DebtManager retain a victim as its effective sender during reentrant crossDeleverage calls against real markets, withdrawing victim positions through attacker-created pools. The proxy was created and initialized with the artifact at 107135785:2, emitting its sole pre-exploit Upgraded event at log 17; the implementation slot and trace select that artifact and its runtime hash matches the declaration. Exactly reports $7,612,038 lost across 117 accounts to the main attacker and copycat.

limitations: The loss uses Exactly's account-level aggregate rather than a separately repriced onchain asset ledger.
